note: Groups are the 127 g-percentiles of Gethin & Fisher-Post (2026), "Government Redistribution and Global Poverty Reduction", data version 2026-09-22: all individuals, with income split equally within couples (WID's 999j unit), ranked by pretax national income. Sizes and average incomes are theirs.

Amounts are in national currency at 2023 prices: Gethin-Fisher values (PPP USD of 2024) times defl (0.950575) times xppp_us (0.778111). Their ReadMe gives the PPP base year as 2023, but xppp_us matches WID's 2024 PPP, so we take the base to be 2024.
Check: total pretax income from Gethin-Fisher is 0.961 times WID's national income for 2023.

Lower thresholds come from WID's tptinc999j for 2023, made nominal and scaled by each group's ratio of Gethin-Fisher's to WID's average income (122 of 126 groups; 4 unscaled where that ratio was unavailable or outside 0.5-2). The bottom group's threshold is set to 0, since Gethin-Fisher's averages don't follow WID's negative incomes.
2 thresholds fell outside the averages of the groups on either side and were moved to the nearer one: p99.6p99.7 p99.999p100.

The current income tax rate by group (effectiveIncomeTaxShareOfIncome) is Gethin-Fisher's personal income tax (tax_dir_pit, their central estimate) over pretax income. Their lower and upper bounds aren't used.
5 groups have non-positive average income; their rate is set to 0.
Data quality Modeled, from WID's data-quality score of 3 (out of 5) on the income thresholds: 4 or 5 is Credible, lower is Modeled.

paramIndividualIncomeTaxCalibratedBaseShareOfIncome (λ): each individual's pretax national income is scaled by λ before the current income tax schedule is applied, with λ chosen so the schedule reproduces Gethin-Fisher's total personal income tax (tax_dir_pit). λ absorbs allowances, deductions, credits, preferential rates, filing-unit effects and evasion, so it is not a measured taxable-income share.

The calibration applies the schedule to group excess curves built from the groups fixture: exact below each group's lower threshold, the midpoint of the upper and lower bounds within a group, and a Pareto tail in the top group (α = a/(a − m)). The model must build its curves the same way to reproduce the target. Target: income tax of 9.50% of pretax income; the schedule applied to all pretax income would raise 22.71%.
OECD Revenue Statistics: personal income tax (code 1100) was 9.14% of GDP in 2023 (central government 9.14%).

Central government: the 2023 statutory schedule from the OECD Tax Database, "Personal income tax (PIT) - central government rates and thresholds" (SDMX dataflow OECD.CTP.TPS,DSD_TAX_PIT@DF_PIT_CENT), for a single person without dependents, applied to wage income. Thresholds are in national currency, nominal 2023. The OECD reports each bracket's upper limit; we store lower limits, starting at 0. 3 brackets, from 9.28% to a top rate of 49.5% above 73,031.
The OECD's sub-central income tax tables have no entry for this country in 2023, so the schedule is the central government's alone.
A basic tax credit of 3,070 is reported separately and is not part of the schedule; like allowances, it is absorbed by calibration.
Capital income (dividends, capital gains, interest) may be taxed under separate rules, e.g. at flat or preferential rates; the general model applies this schedule only.
